Existing surveys largely examine self-improvement mechanisms and on-device learning separately, providing limited guidance on how update reliability and device costs should be assessed together. items.summary: Abstract Baryon acoustic oscillations from DESI DR2, combined with the cosmic microwave background and type Ia supernovae, prefer dark energy that is evolving away from w = −1. items.title: Heterophase-Engineered Cs3Cu2I5/CsCu2I3 Memristors with Two-Step Resistive Switching.
items.summary: The quest for energy-efficient memory technologies is critically hindered by the performance gap between high-performing but toxic lead-based perovskites and their environmentally benign yet less reliable lead-free counterparts. Here, we address this challenge by engineering the controlled coexistence of crystallographically 0D Cs3Cu2I5 and 1D CsCu2I3 phases using a scalable, hot-air-assisted process. The resulting heterophase architecture produces composition-dependent structural, interfacial, and chemical environments that strongly influence resistive-switching behavior. items.title: Photoactive Nanocomposite Dielectric-Driven Low-Power All-Optical Organic Synaptic Transistors.
items.summary: Artificial optical synapses featuring low-energy consumption, high speed, and noise tolerance are critical for visual neuromorphic electronics. items.title: Conductive filament dynamics in memristive sensors: from resistive switching mechanisms to multifunctional sensing applications.
items.summary: With advances in sensor technology, various sensors are being widely applied, becoming an indispensable part of modern life. However, constrained by inherent sensing mechanisms, certain performance limitations remain difficult to improve through conventional modification methods. Herein, we focus on memristors for various sensing applications, summarizing how their resistive switching effect enables the modulation of device performance. items.summary: Escalating energy demands for high-performance machine learning have sparked growing interest in unconventional computing paradigms rooted in physical systems. items.title: Integration and annotation of spatial multi-omic data with DIRAC.
items.summary: Spatial multi-omic technologies measure multiple molecular layers within intact tissues. Two central challenges are vertical integration, which combines different molecular modalities, and horizontal integration, which aligns cell types across studies. Here we show domain invariant representation through adaptive calibration (DIRAC), a geometric deep learning model that unifies these tasks in a generalized domain adaptation framework. items.title: When, Where, and How Experience Becomes Structure: Mechanisms for Recursive Self-Improvement in LLM Agents
items.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) studies how AI systems modify themselves and carry those changes into the generation of subsequent improvements. items.summary: We present an exploration-first strategy for intramolecular conformational search. items.title: Duality of root-dominated net soil organic carbon gain and mycelium-mediated carbon loss in hyper-arid afforestation.
items.summary: Afforestation regulates soil organic carbon (SOC) sequestration via plant- and microbial-derived carbon (C) inputs, but root- and mycelium-derived C inputs differ in quantity, turnover, and stabilization mechanisms, and these differences may shift as stands develop. items.title: Learning inhibitor interactions from protein deep mutational scanning data and deep learning models
items.summary: Recent advances in protein language models, geometric deep learning, and structure prediction frameworks have the potential to accelerate computational drug discovery. items.summary: Open-vocabulary 3D scene graph generation aims to predict 3D objects and their predicates beyond the annotated label space. items.title: From Harness Optimization to Recursive Self-Improvement: A Survey of Language Model Agents
items.summary: Language-model agents rely on harnesses that govern tool use, context, memory, and execution. items.title: AI4AI: Toward AI-Discovered Superintelligence
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping how AI itself is developed. From designing learning algorithms to automating research workflows and evaluation, this expanding role has fueled the rapid growth of AI for AI (AI4AI).
